messages:
Lina: FYI we're scheduling tenant backfill for profile_flags (online alter) at 02:00 UTC. Small slices; will route low-write tenants first.
Marc: What's fallback if DB CPU spikes?
Lina: Plan: deploy-bot will pause and reroute to read-only replica + enable fallback route to legacy service. Manual holdpoint before ramp.
deploy-bot: Deploybot: HOLDPOINT set at "pre-ramp". Operator approval required to proceed.
Nina: Recommend pin web-service to v3.0.2 to avoid reading new boolean field. I'll pin.
infra-bot: infra-bot: feature flag and route configured for fallback; KV cache warm-up available.
Marc: Rollback steps: 1) pause backfill 2) flip traffic to legacy (deploy-bot reroute) 3) drain queues and revert feature flag.
Oscar: Add watch: CPU > 75% for 2m -> PAUSE. Also watch replica_lag > 20s -> PAUSE.
Lina: Canary will run 5% tenants for 20m. Oncall please ack.
Marc: acked; will monitor p99 and CPU.
deploy-bot: Deploybot: HOLDPOINT cleared after approval by Lina at 02:06 UTC. Canary started.
Nina: small p99 bump at 02:09, normalized by 02:12. No queue growth.
Oscar: CPU spiked to 78% at 02:15 on db-primary, triggered watch -> deploy-bot auto-paused slices. Resuming at lower parallelism.
deploy-bot: Deploybot: PAUSE triggered by cpu_watch. Paused 02:15. Lowering parallelism and resuming.
Lina: Lower parallelism to 2 workers and resume. Monitoring.
Marc: After change, CPU steady, p99 okay. Proceeding to full ramp over next 40m.
Nina: Unpin scheduled for 06:00 UTC.
Lina: Full rollout completed by 03:12 UTC. Logs archived s3://redwood-ops/migrations/profile_flags/1760012345
Marc: Post-run: increase CPU watch threshold to 80% for noisy tenants and add per-tenant slice cap.
Lina: Thanks all, closing thread. :thumbsup:
